railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_1: First, use a Create Train Signal on a track to select its position and direction.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_2: Place that Create signal beside the track. It controls the railway signal section.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_3: Place the Railward signal directly above it. The tall signal needs four blocks of free height.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_4: The Railward block searches 1 to 4 blocks straight down from its base for a Create signal. Leave gaps or hide the source below the surface.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_5: The compact ground signal connects in exactly the same way.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_6: Use a wrench on the Railward base to rotate it in 16 steps. Its facing does not change the track direction selected by the Create signal.
railward.ponder.signal_placement.text_7: Railward repeats the Create signal's lights. Track links, signal modes and redstone control belong to the Create signal below.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_1: Green repeats Create's clear signal: the protected section is available.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_2: Red repeats Create's stop signal: the section is occupied, reserved, or blocked by redstone.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_3: Yellow repeats Create's chain-signal warning: only some routes ahead are available. It is not an automatic speed limit.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_4: A brief flashing red light means the Create signal is invalid. Check its track connection.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_5: No lights? Check for a Create signal directly below the Railward base, no more than four blocks away.
railward.ponder.signal_aspects.text_6: Create signals guide scheduled trains. When driving manually, watch and obey the lights yourself.
railward.ponder.ground_signal_aspects.te: Blue is the ground signal's stop light. It repeats a red Create signal.
White repeats a green Create signal: the protected section is available.
A yellow Create signal also produces white here. This two-light head does not distinguish green from yellow.
Brief blue flashes mean the Create signal is invalid. Check its track connection.
Without a Create signal 1 to 4 blocks directly below, both lights stay off.
The compact head changes the appearance only. Create still controls train routing and signal sections.
railward.ponder.cistern_hatch.text_1: The Cistern Hatch on the train and the stationary Fluid Terminal work as a pair, like Create's Portable Fluid Interface.
railward.ponder.cistern_hatch.text_2: Place the terminal directly above the hatch, at the same X and Z. Its block must be 1 or 2 blocks higher: zero or one empty block between them.
railward.ponder.cistern_hatch.text_3: On connection, the hose extends to the hatch and its lid opens automatically.
railward.ponder.cistern_hatch.text_4: A hatch accesses the fluid storage of its own carriage. Tanks on other carriages need their own hatch.
railward.ponder.cistern_hatch.text_5: As the pair separates, the hose retracts and the hatch lid closes.
railward.ponder.fluid_terminal.text_1: The Fluid Terminal and Cistern Hatch form a fluid-transfer pair, analogous to Create's Portable Fluid Interface.
railward.ponder.fluid_terminal.text_2: The terminal belongs directly above the hatch, 1 or 2 blocks higher. This leaves zero or one empty block between their blocks.
railward.ponder.fluid_terminal.text_3: One connection handles both loading and unloading. The hose and hatch lid automatically follow the connection state.
railward.ponder.fluid_terminal.text_4: The comparator reports the connection: 15 when connected and 0 when disconnected, regardless of how full the cistern is.
railward.ponder.fluid_terminal.text_5: Redstone power disables the terminal. Removing the signal allows the pair to connect again.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_1: Bulk Cargo Containers of the same colour combine into one rectangular storage.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_2: Fill the whole footprint: a square base makes a wide open container.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_3: Rectangular bases work too: length, width and height do not have to be equal.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_4: Right-click the top with matching container blocks to add a complete layer. You need enough blocks for that layer. Maximum size: 11 by 11 by 16.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_5: Different colours stay separate even when they touch. Each colour keeps its own walls and inventory.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_6: Throw items into the open top. The container collects them; one storage holds one cargo type.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_7: Right-click with an empty hand to take one stack of cargo.
railward.ponder.bulk_storage.text_8: Hoppers and other blocks that interact with inventories can insert and extract cargo too.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.header: Loading and unloading a bulk wagon
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_1: A bulk wagon is served by an overhead hatch for loading and a bunker below for unloading.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_2: Place the loading hatch directly above the cargo container, 1 to 3 blocks higher than its top layer.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_3: The hatch takes cargo from the inventory directly above it and feeds the wagon below. No separate portable interface is needed.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_4: For unloading, a hatch in the wagon floor must line up above the bunker. Their blocks can be 1 to 3 blocks apart vertically.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_5: The bunker exposes the wagon inventory. Extract items from it with a hopper or another inventory-interacting block to unload the wagon.
railward.ponder.bulk_transport.text_6: When the wagon leaves, the connection ends. The cargo already unloaded remains in the receiving storage.
railward.ponder.coupler_automatic.text_1: Place couplers at the outer ends of the trains, facing each other at the same height.
railward.ponder.coupler_automatic.text_2: Both trains must be aligned on the same track network, entirely on straight, level track. The receiving train must be stopped.
railward.ponder.coupler_automatic.text_3: Remove schedules from both trains before coupling. Automatic coupling must be enabled in the server configuration.
railward.ponder.coupler_automatic.text_4: Approach slowly. Coupling will not engage above the configured speed limit.
railward.ponder.coupler_automatic.text_5: The couplers join the two trains automatically. The locomotive can now pull the wagon as one train.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.header: Coupling and uncoupling with a wrench
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_1: For manual coupling, stop both trains close together with their couplers facing each other. Keep both trains aligned on the same straight, level track network and remove their schedules.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_2: Right-click either facing coupler with Create's wrench to join the trains. Only one click is needed.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_3: The joined carriages move together. The same wrench interaction also separates carriages within a train.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_4: Stop the train, then right-click a coupler between the carriages with the wrench to split it at that connection.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_5: Uncoupling also works with a paused schedule; an active schedule must be paused first. Coupling requires both schedules to be removed.
railward.ponder.coupler_manual.text_6: A freshly uncoupled pair will not immediately reconnect automatically. Move the trains apart before approaching again.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_3: Give locomotive trains distinct names; leave #001-style names for automatically numbered stock. Naming priority depends on train controls, not on name prefixes.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_6: Manual coupling keeps the name of the part with train controls when only one part has them: L-01 + W-01 becomes L-01.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_7: Automatic coupling always keeps the moving train's name, even if the other train also has controls.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_10: After splitting, the part with controls keeps the name. A detached part without controls gets a free number, for example #001. Its old name is not restored.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_13: If both parts have controls, or neither does, manual coupling keeps the clicked train's name. Click M-02's coupler to keep M-02.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_16: When both separated parts have controls, the first part in the train's carriage order keeps the name; the other gets a free number.
railward.ponder.coupler_names.text_19: If neither separated part has controls, both get free numbers. Numbers such as #001 and #002 are generated automatically, skipping names already in use.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_1: Matching Cistern blocks join horizontally. Their axes must point in the same direction.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_2: For a wider cistern, fill a complete 3 by 3 cross-section, including its centre. A hollow shell will not combine.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_3: Right-click either end with matching Cistern blocks to add a whole cross-section. A 3 by 3 section needs 9 blocks and free space.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_4: The largest diameter is 5 blocks: fill a solid 5 by 5 cross-section. Adding another section consumes 25 matching blocks.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_5: All three diameters, 1, 3 and 5 blocks, support lengths from 1 to 11 blocks. The maximum size is 5 by 5 by 11.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_6: Different colours stay separate even when they touch. Each cistern keeps its own fluid storage.
railward.ponder.cistern_building.text_7: Cisterns can extend along either horizontal axis. Face along the desired axis when placing their blocks.
railward.ponder.cistern_connections.head: Connecting pipes to a cistern
railward.ponder.cistern_connections.text: On a 3-block-wide cistern, connect pipes to the centre block of either end.
Side connections use the middle row; top and bottom connections use the centre line. These connections must be between the two end sections.
A 5-block-wide cistern accepts end connections anywhere in the central 3 by 3 area. Its side, top and bottom connections follow the same centre-line rule.
A 1-block-wide cistern accepts pipes only at its two ends.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_1: Mount Buffer Lights on a locomotive's end face. The block behind them provides support.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_2: Right-click with a wrench to cycle through 13 housing styles. Every style uses the same automatic lighting rules.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_3: Right-click a Railward wall panel with Buffer Lights to mount them directly on it. Wrench-click the lights themselves to change their style.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_4: In the direction of the selected controller, Buffer Lights shine white. At the rear they shine red.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_5: Select the opposite controller and the colours swap: white ahead, red at the rear. This also works with an active train schedule.
railward.ponder.buffer_lights.text_6: Buffer Lights are off outside an assembled train or when there is no active manual or scheduled control. Simply stopping does not switch them off.
railward.ponder.locomotive_spotlight.tex: Mount a Spotlight on the locomotive's end face. Right-click it with a wrench to switch between the small and large housings.
You can also right-click a Railward wall panel with a Spotlight to mount it directly. Wrench-click the mounted spotlight to change its size.
The spotlight in the direction of the selected controller lights the track. The rear spotlight stays off.
Select the opposite controller to switch the active spotlight. Direction is selected by manual train controls or an active schedule.
To switch spotlights off independently, set a Contraption Controls filter to the Spotlight item. Toggling that control disables spotlights without changing Buffer Lights.
Toggle the control again to restore the spotlight for the current direction. Without active train control, both spotlights remain off.
This controller combines throttle, brake and reverser. One controller can drive a train in either direction.
With the reverser set to forward, Buffer Lights are white in the selected direction and red at the rear.
Before changing direction, stop completely and release both throttle and brake. The reverser cannot switch while either input is held.
Press the reverser key (R by default) while controlling the train to select reverse travel. The white and red Buffer Lights swap ends.
Press the reverser key again at a standstill to return to forward travel. Both directions use this same controller.
When train control ends, the levers return to neutral. Without active manual or scheduled control, the Buffer Lights switch off.
railward.ponder.rail_crossing_signal.hea: Setting up a rail crossing signal
railward.ponder.rail_crossing_signal.tex: With the Rail Crossing Signal in hand, right-click the Relay Cabinet that monitors the track section.
The selected cabinet is highlighted. Place the signal beside the crossing.
While the track section is free, the signal stays dark and silent.
When the track section is occupied, the red lamps flash alternately and the warning sounds.
Once the whole train clears the section, both lamps go out and the warning stops.
Right-click the white square on the front of the signal to open its settings.
Choose no sign, a single-track sign, or a multi-track sign. The sound can be set to Small Bell, Bell, or Siren.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_1: Face the intended direction of travel and right-click the rail with the Speed Limit Sign in hand.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_2: Place the sign beside the selected rail. The track marker shows the direction in which the limit applies.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_3: Hold right-click on the small panel below the number to set the limit in km/h.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_4: When the front of the train passes the marked point in that direction, the sign sets the train's speed limit.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_5: On the return trip the train keeps its current limit. The last setting stays in effect until the speed limit is changed again.
railward.ponder.speed_sign.text_6: A wrench turns the sign face. Its direction of action comes from the rail selection.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_1: Face the intended direction of travel and right-click the rail with the Whistle Sign in hand.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_2: Place the sign beside the selected rail. The track marker shows which direction triggers the whistle.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_3: For an automatic whistle, the train needs a whistle or horn and a conductor running an active schedule.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_4: The conductor sounds the train's whistle as the front of the train passes the marker in the selected direction.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_5: For a whistle on the return trip, link another sign while facing the opposite direction.
railward.ponder.whistle_sign.text_6: A wrench turns the sign face. Its direction of action comes from the rail selection.
